Alice M.: Heads up — p99 latency jumped ~40% on api-runtime-prod after the driver 12.3.1 rollout ~10:22 UTC. Traces show the kernel selector started preferring flash_kernel_v2 for short sequences (<=64) which is slower on these cards.
Rafael G.: Confirmed on canary. Throughput dipped too, and we saw increased KV-cache evictions correlated with the slow kernel path. p50 unchanged.
deploy-bot: deploy redwood-runtime:release/2026-03-18/12.3.1 completed on 12 hosts (region us-west2).
Priya K.: Can you paste the profiler snippet (kernel names + launch times)? curious whether it's launch overhead or the kernel itself being slower. Also what GPU driver version exactly?
Alice M.: Paste below (from perf-trace on host api-07):
```
# profiler excerpt
kernel: matmul_smallseq_v1    time_ms: 0.85  (was typical)
kernel: flash_kernel_v2       time_ms: 2.9   <-- new hot path
kernel: kv_lookup_and_update  time_ms: 0.45
kernel: softmax_block         time_ms: 0.6
// seq_len distrib: 8: 48%, 16: 22%, 32: 18%, 64: 12%
// driver: NVIDIA 535.54.03
```
Priya K.: That flash_kernel_v2 microbenchmarks great for long sequences but it seems driver change altered launch latency for the short-tile path. Combined with our batching heuristic that biases larger batches for these seq lengths, we’re getting suboptimal packing and more KV cache churn.
Evan S.: Quick mitigation: can we force kernel selector to prefer matmul_smallseq_v1 for seq <= 64 via env override? I can push a runtime config change for Dedicated pools.
Alice M.: I'm applying runtime override now to prod route `text.generate` using `RUNTIME_KERNEL_POLICY=prefer_smallseq` (temp). Will monitor.
Alice M.: Update 10m after change — p99 back near baseline. Numbers: baseline p99 ~220ms, spike ~320ms, after override ~235ms. CPU and GPU util normalized.
Rafael G.: Good catch. We need a regression test: kernel-selector stability after driver/driver-lib updates + a small micro-bench that exercises seq<=64 distribution. Also add an alert when kernel selection mix shifts >20% from historical.
Priya K.: I'll open a perf-ops PR: add a micro-benchmark in perf-ci (seq dist + fake KV hits) and a Grafana alert for `kernel_selector_mix{model="*"}` divergence. Also propose adding a post-driver-upgrade canary that runs the microbench on a single host.
Evan S.: For Dedicated customers we should document the env override workaround and add it to runbooks. I filed RUNBOOK-217.
Alice M.: Filing a short incident note for postmortem; tagging perf/regress. Root cause hypothesis: driver 535.* changed kernel launch characteristics causing selector to prefer flash_kernel_v2 for small tiles; our selector heuristics lack a post-driver stability guard.
Rafael G.: Follow-ups: (1) add selector unit tests that simulate increased launch latency, (2) add selector feature flag to enable conservative mode automatically after infra upgrades, (3) coordinate with infra to roll driver hotfix or blacklist flash_kernel_v2 until we vet it.
Priya K.: I'll draft the PR and test harness. ETA EOD.
Alice M.: Thanks all. I'll paste the canary traces and the p99 chart into the incident doc. :thumbsup:
